source: Phrase-only curriculum: B1 /θ/ and /ð/ in everyday collocations, progressive sentences and minimal-pair contrast drills (/θ/–/s/, /ð/–/d/, /θ/–/t/, /w/–/v/). Builds on the B1 /θ/ and B2 /ð/ topics of English_Accent_Training_Actual_Program.md.

sections.label: Everyday phrase
sections.description: Short collocations and work phrases (3–5 words) that put /θ/ or /ð/ in a natural chunk.

sections.label: B1 sentence
sections.description: Progressive 6–10 word sentences with several /θ/ and /ð/ sounds in connected speech.

sections.label: Contrast drill
sections.description: Minimal-pair sentences that force a clean switch between commonly confused sounds.

exercises.cue: 'Think' is voiceless /θ/ — air only. 'the' is voiced /ð/ — same tongue, add a buzz.
Three /θ/ starts in a row: reset the tongue tip to your teeth before each one.
Round the lips for /w/, finish 'worth' with air at the teeth, then glide into a voiced 'the'.
Don't let the final /θ/ in 'teeth' turn into /t/ or /s/ before 'and'.
'Breathe' ends in voiced /ð/ — feel the buzz on your tongue as you link into 'in'.
Two voiced /ð/ sounds: keep the tongue light at the teeth, never a hard /d/.

exercises.target_text: I thought about thirty-three things this morning.
exercises.cue: Four voiceless /θ/ starts, then a voiced /ð/ in 'this' — keep each one airy as you speed up.

exercises.target_text: The author shared his thoughtful perspective on the theme.
exercises.cue: 'The' is voiced /ð/, 'author', 'thoughtful' and 'theme' are voiceless /θ/ — same tongue, different buzz.

exercises.target_text: Her healthy tooth was throbbing throughout the night.
exercises.cue: Watch the final /θ/ in 'tooth' before the /w/ of 'was'.

exercises.target_text: We need a thorough method to measure team growth.
exercises.cue: Keep the /θ/ in 'method' and the final /θ/ in 'growth' — they are easy to drop at speed.

exercises.target_text: They walked together through the chilly autumn weather.
Although it was difficult, they found a worthwhile pathway.
exercises.cue: 'Although', 'they' are voiced /ð/; 'worthwhile' and 'pathway' hide a voiceless /θ/ before a /w/.

exercises.target_text: I think the kitchen sink is clean.
exercises.cue: think = tongue at the teeth; sink = tongue behind the teeth.

exercises.target_text: Take a deep breath and pass the test.
exercises.cue: breath ends with air between the teeth; pass and test end with a sharp hiss behind them.

exercises.target_text: They dare to go there together.
exercises.cue: they = soft buzz at the teeth; dare = a quick tap behind the teeth.

exercises.target_text: Three tall trees grew along the track.
exercises.cue: three = friction you can stretch; tall, trees, track = a quick stop.

exercises.target_text: We went to view the very wide valley.
exercises.cue: /w/ = rounded lips, no teeth. /v/ = top teeth touch the lower lip.
